measurement: close before print to close after first full session following

names.notes: Reported Q1 FY2027 after close 2026-09-02: adjusted EPS -$0.20, beat consensus of roughly -$0.25 to -$0.26; revenue $52.4M, a narrow beat, down ~25% y/y. Q2 FY27 revenue guided to $51-55M vs ~$56.6M consensus (below Street) and FY27 revenue guided to $210-240M -- several outlets initially framed this as a several-percent after-hours/premarket decline. By Thursday's regular close the stock was actually up 3.61% versus Wednesday's close, below the 11.3% unsigned expected move and below the low end of its own 5.7-21.8% band. The Neutral / No Edge call scores a hit under the below-expected-move convention. The red-team's reversal case here was itself the bullish one -- a heavily shorted, exhausted-seller setup (34.65% of float short, 9.65 days to cover) where an in-line Q1 with a reaffirmed FY27 range would be enough to force covering even on a soft Q2 guide -- and that is broadly what happened: the weak guide did not sink the stock. The stage-2 preliminary read (-22, bearish) called the wrong direction, though the move was small enough that the sign flip carries limited information.

Reported Q2 FY2027 after close 2026-09-02: adjusted EPS $0.62 vs $0.45 consensus (beat), revenue $1.55B vs ~$1.48B consensus (beat, product revenue +37% y/y). Full-year product revenue guidance raised to $6.07B (36% growth) from $5.84B (31% growth). Stock had sold off ~4% into the print, then jumped ~22% after hours and settled at +16.56% by Thursday's close, breaking the 14.0% unsigned expected move by a narrow margin. The Neutral / No Edge call is a miss under the below-expected-move convention, though it lands inside its wide 7.0-38.3% band. The red-team's specific reversal case -- 'a beat-and-raise that sells off anyway because the buyside bar (implied ~33%+ growth) is above the sell-side bar' -- did not fire; the raise was strong enough (36% vs a Q1 print of 34%) to be read as acceleration, not deceleration, and the stock ripped instead. The stage-2 preliminary read (-10, bearish) called the wrong direction on the day's largest panelled miss by magnitude.

Reported fiscal Q3 2026 after close 2026-09-02: non-GAAP EPS $3.32 vs $2.45 consensus (beat by ~35.5%), revenue $29.591B vs ~$29.4B consensus (beat, +86% y/y). Q4 FY26 revenue guided to $34.8B vs ~$35.03B consensus -- guidance came in just below expectations despite the enormous beat, and FY27/FY28 AI-revenue framing ($115B, then $230B) was not enough to offset it. Shares gapped down as much as ~6-7% intraday before partially recovering to close -2.74%. The stage-2 preliminary read (+6, weakly bullish) called the wrong direction, though weakly held (score of only 6).

Reported Q2 FY2026 after close 2026-09-02: EPS $3.70 vs $3.08 consensus (beat, but ~$1.80/share of the beat was a tariff-refund benefit), revenue $2.097B, down ~3% y/y and roughly in line to slightly light. Full-year outlook reaffirmed; a $439M non-cash goodwill impairment was also recorded. Shares closed essentially flat, +0.24%, a near-noise move with no meaningful reaction either way. The stage-2 preliminary read (-15, bearish) is scored a technical miss on sign, but the move is close enough to zero that this is a low-information data point, similar to BILL on 2026-08-19.

Reported fiscal Q1 FY2027 after close 2026-09-02: non-GAAP EPS $2.58 vs $2.12 consensus (beat by ~21.5%, +66% y/y), revenue $2.03B vs ~$1.84B consensus (beat by ~10.2%, +30% y/y). Full-year revenue and EPS guidance both raised well above prior consensus. Coverage describes an initial sell-the-news dip before the stock recovered to close +2.55%. The stage-2 preliminary read (-10, bearish) called the wrong direction on a clean beat-and-raise.

Reported Q2 FY2026 before open 2026-09-03: adjusted EPS $0.95 vs ~$0.77-0.78 consensus (beat), revenue $1.61B, a slight miss vs ~$1.62B consensus though +10.4% y/y. Full-year net sales and EPS guidance both raised, but the raise leaned heavily on >$140M of one-time tariff refunds in Q2 operating income, and the Q3 operating-income guide disappointed. Shares gapped down at the open and kept falling through the session to close -13.17% near the day's low. The stage-2 preliminary read (+12, bullish) called the wrong direction -- the largest single-name preliminary miss (by magnitude) across all three runs scored today.
